text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The first meeting of the new cabinet suggested to parliament to merge the economy, energy and industry and trade ministries into one new national economy ministry, to found a european affairs ministry and to merge the forestry and agriculture ministries.

- Planned oil terminal Butinges Terminalas intends to make its fourth issue of shares in the near future. It was planned to boost the share capital to 185 million litas but the company has only got 72 million litas so far.

- The privatisation agency proposed the sale of Lithuanian Airlines, the Klaipeda West Ship Repair company, the Klaipeda Sea Cargo Company and the Klaipeda Ship Repair Company next year but the final decision must be taken by the government. The chairman of the agency said that everything not forbidden by the constitution should be privatised.
- Diplomats from EU nations were mostly interested in Lithuania's borders with neighbouring countries during a dinner with President Algirdas Brazauskas.
- It is planned to triple to 33 million litas the allocations to the Defence ministry for the Partnership for Peace (PFP) program in the budget of next year.
- Deposits in Lithuanian banks increased more than two times during last three years and in October 1996 were estimated at 4.58 billion litas.
- The reserves of convertible currency in the central bank were estimated at $764 million and were nearly three times higher than in 1993.
- GDP was 1,470 litas per capita during the first half of 1996.

- The planners of a new monetary policy at the central bank have not answered the question of why they do not like the present calm in the money market and why the litas should be pegged to the German mark, the president of the Free Market Economy Institute Elena Leontjeva says in an interview. She said that the reform plan was very concrete and there was an impression that the currency board, criticised by many, is being rehabilitated.
- Sociologists predict that the population decrease over the last three years will continue. Lithuania had 3.712 million inhabitants in 1996, compared to 3.736 million in 1993.
- Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas was positive over the the schedule of planned NATO expansion.
- Gediminas Vagnorius returned to the government building after an absence of 1,602 days to start the first meeting of his cabinet. Vagnorius was previously prime minister in 1991-92.
